While everyone agrees races have historically mixed, the time periods it was over were so slow that genetic drift has pushed various relatively isolated populations apart, enough that people from one area are measurably distinct from people in another. We aren't different species, we can still interbreed and we have a lot of common heritage, but the genetic diversity is real. That's basically what race is, genetically isolated groups that have become distinct, but not enough to start speciation, the best analog being breeds of dogs that vary greatly in size, colour, shape of the nose, disposition and so on, while still being the same species canine familiaris.

'Racial purity' in that regard can be measured from the various inheritable traits that have developed in different genetically isolated populations, with the most racially pure having a long history in a region, dating back to the formation of those traits, and the least racially pure having traits from a variety of groups in mixed concentrations. Interbreeding races will naturally mix these traits, until the original genetic diversity is averaged out.
